studyMetadata.title: Visualization Literacy Assessment
studyMetadata.description: An assessment that measures one's comprehension of graphs

response.prompt: After which two meals are blood glucose levels most similar? (Select 2)
What would the person's blood glucose level look like if they skipped their snack?
options: Blood sugar would remain constant after lunch and then spike after dinner.
Blood glucose would continue to decrease after lunch and then spike after dinner.
Blood glucose would still increase at the same time.
There would be no change to the graph.

response.prompt: Choose the best generalization about the graph:
options: The person’s blood sugar is consistently at dangerous levels.
The person’s blood sugar is at dangerous levels more than half of the time.
The person’s blood sugar is at dangerous levels only a few times during the day.
The person’s blood sugar is never at a dangerous level.

response.prompt: When does the person's blood glucose reach a dangerously high level?
When does it look like the person had lunch?
How often does the person maintain a healthy blood sugar level?
Which meal causes the person's blood glucose to spike to its highest level?
Why does the snack cause the smallest increase in blood glucose compared to the other meals?
options: The body becomes more resistant to glucose as the day goes on.
Blood glucose levels only rise significantly in the morning.
Snacks usually contain fewer calories or carbohydrates than full meals.
The snack was eaten at the same time as dinner.

response.prompt: What statement best describes the overall trend of the graph?
options: Blood glucose always rises after eating and then falls back down.
Blood glucose levels stay flat throughout the day.
Blood glucose decreases after meals and increases between them.
Blood glucose remains in the same range at all times.

response.prompt: Approximately what time does the person’s blood glucose level drop to its lowest point?
If this person had diabetes and needed to avoid dangerous blood sugar spikes, which meal would they most likely need to reduce or change?
Check off the correct generalization that can be made about the data.
options: Blood glucose spikes a normal amount after meals.
Blood glucose spikes very slightly after meals.
Blood glucose stays the same after meals.
There is no clear blood glucose pattern.
